2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3.

The petitioners have filed this writ petition seeking direction to the opposite parties to return the un-acquired land measuring Ac.4.99 decimals out of Sabik Plot nos.670, 671, 675, 676, 694 and 697 under Sabik Khata No.46 of Mouza- Durgapur in the district of Sundargarh, for which no compensation has been awarded in favour of the recorded tenant, who was the common ancestor of the petitioners, or in the alternative acquire the aforesaid lands as per Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and pay due and adequate compensation within a stipulated time.

sentences.text: 4. Mr. P.K. Nayak, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that Ac.11.37 dec. of land of the petitioners has been notified for acquisition and out of that only Ac.5.13 dec. has been acquired and compensation has been paid.
But so far as the rest land, i.e., Ac.4.99 dec. of land is concerned, no acquisition has been made.
Therefore, the petitioners seek for direction to the opposite parties to return the un-acquired land or pay compensation for the same.
5. Ms. S. Pattnaik, learned Addl.
Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties contended that the acquisition was made in the year 1954 and now the petitioners have made prayer to return their land.
But fact remains that the land was acquired and the same was utilized for the purpose of establishment of Steel Authority of India.
As such, the balance land, i.e., Ac.4.99 dec. has been recorded in the Government khata, for which compensation amount has already been paid.

sentences.text: Mr. G. Mishra, learned Senior Counsel appearing along with Mr. J.R. Deo, learned counsel appearing for opposite party no.5 contended that for the purpose of establishment of Rourkela Steel Plant whatever land has been acquired by the State Government, compensation has already been paid.
Therefore, the petitioners have no right to claim the benefit at this belated stage.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that Ac.11.37 dec. of land has been acquired, for which compensation amount has been determined and, as such, the same has already been paid to the petitioners.

Mr. P.K. Nayak, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that out of Ac.11.37 dec. of land only Ac.5.13 dec. of land has been acquired and for balance Ac.4.99 dec. of land, no compensation has been paid and, as such, the said land still remains with the Government.
But fact remains, the compensation amount has already been determined by the authority and, as such, the same has been paid to the petitioners.
Therefore, if at all for any acquired land compensation amount has not been paid, the petitioners could have approached the authority at the earliest.

Though the land was acquired in the year 1954, the petitioners have approached this Court in the year 2021 stating that for acquisition of land they are entitled to get compensation or refund of the said land, which cannot be entertained at this stage.
As such, the writ petition filed by the petitioner at the belated stage absolutely suffers from delay and laches.

In any case, since the land has been acquired and the compensation amount has not been paid, the petitioners have to approach the appropriate forum instead of approaching this Court by filing the present writ petition.
8. In such view of the matter, this writ petition stands disposed of permitting the petitioners to approach the appropriate forum in accordance with law.
